summary: I built option (b): Cancel still waits for the scan to finish, and it never abandons the scan thread. Two seconds after Cancel, a new StoppingDetail line under "Stopping..." shows a wait message. The wording comes from a pure function, StoppingWait.For, which is linked into Core.Tests so its boundaries are pinned there. The line updates on the existing 250 ms progress tick and is cleared in the scan's single finally block. I moved the stall rig into Rig/SmbRig.cs and added a machine-wide mutex, so two rig runs cannot share 127.0.0.1. Under that lock the rig removes rig-shaped mappings a killed run left behind. The rig also runs as a self-contained StallRig.exe. The hook now logs the Stopping state and a `returned` stamp, and can time Cancel and Close from the rig's armed marker. WindowCases.ps1 gains a C-006 check that the line never appears on an ordinary cancel, plus four opt-in cases behind -IncludeNetwork: N-001 (wait line), N-002 (closing the window ends the app), N-003 (a second rig run waits or fails with an error that says why) and N-004 (a killed run's leftover mapping). The default suite passes 149/149, the default window run passes all 15 cases, all 8 window mutants still fail for their planted reason, and Fitness passes all 25 rules. N-001 to N-004 were not run, because they change this machine's SMB mappings and nobody has recorded consent for that.

files.why: The wording as a pure function of time since Cancel: null under 2 s or for a negative span, the 'minute or more' line from 2 s to under 90 s, no estimate from 90 s. ASCII only. No WPF, file or drive calls.
StoppingDetail: a wrapping TextBlock under ScanningTitle, collapsed by default.

OnCancel starts a nullable Stopwatch. Each progress tick calls ShowStopping, which sets the line from the clock alone. EndStopping sits next to _timer.Stop() in StartScan's one finally, before ScanningPanel collapses. The scanner is untouched.
Compiles src/FsAnalyser.App/StoppingWait.cs by link. There is no reference to the App project.

Default-run boundary tests: -5 s, -1 ms, 0, 1.999 s, 2 s, 89.999 s, 90 s, 3600 s, a gap of one tick either side of each boundary, TimeSpan.MinValue, flooring, and a check that the text is ASCII and carries no bound or frequency on the wait.

LoopbackShare and StallingFileStore moved out of StalledShareTests with no xUnit dependency. Adds RigLock, a named mutex held for the rig's lifetime. Under the lock the rig sweeps leftover mappings matching exactly \\127.0.0.1\fsa plus 8 hex digits (IsRigMapping). This is the only file that may run New-SmbMapping or Remove-SmbMapping.
The rig classes were removed from this file. Test behaviour and the Network=SMB-LOOPBACK trait are unchanged.

Default-run tests of M1 that need no share: a second holder waits for the first; a live holder in another process makes the next run time out with a message saying why; after that holder is killed with TerminateProcess, the waiting run and a new run get the lock at once; the sweep filter never matches a person's mapping such as \\100.109.48.75\collab.
Console built outside the slnx that compiles Rig/SmbRig.cs by link. It uses the same SMBLibrary package versions as Core.Tests and is self-contained win-x64.

`StallRig.exe --marker <file> [--wait-sec n]` builds its tree next to the marker file and prints the UNC root. It writes the marker when the listing of hung stalls. When stdin closes it releases the server, unmaps only its own mapping and exits 0. It exits 1 on a mapping failure or lock timeout and 2 on bad arguments.

After any Cancel the hook presses, it logs a `stopping` line every 250 ms from the UI thread, a `returned` line when ScanningPanel collapses, and a final line at Dispatcher.ShutdownStarted. With FSA_HOOK_ARMED set it waits for the rig's marker, presses Cancel at FSA_HOOK_CANCEL_DELAY_MS (unset means no Cancel) and closes at FSA_HOOK_CLOSE_DELAY_MS while the scan is still running, logging closed and UTC stamps. When FSA_HOOK_ARMED is unset, the actions are the same as before.

C-006 now also asserts the scan returned within 2 s, that no stopping line shows the wait line, and that a final line was written. Adds -IncludeNetwork with N-001 to N-004 plus helpers: Read-Stopping, CheckWaitLine, CheckCloseEscape, Start-/Stop-/Kill-StallRig and Update-StallRig. Network cases not run are reported NOT RUN, and a network case named on its own without the switch exits 2.

O-012: the abandon rule loses its leading \b and gains a pattern for a scan started and awaited against the token in one expression. O-011: the SMB-mapping rule is split into tests/**/*.cs, tests/**/*.ps1 and eng/**/*.ps1, and adds New-SmbGlobalMapping, net use and WNet(Add|Cancel)Connection. SmbRig.cs stays the only exception.

Decision record in the section that already documents the stalled shape: what the line says, why abandoning was rejected (spike figures), what is unmeasured (real disconnects, and 'Closing the window quits at once' resting on the rig), the person's protocol including a timed Close per mode, what would reopen the question, how it is tested (the default run proves only that the line does not appear), and how the rig isolates runs.

obligations.how: C-006 now checks the stop run's hook log. It must contain exactly one `returned` line under 2000 ms (12 to 14 ms measured), a final line written at shutdown, detail `-` on every stopping line, and the title 'Stopping...' on every line. `WindowCases.ps1 -Case C-006` passed, and so did `-Case All`.

N-001 (CheckWaitLine) checks four things. The Cancel press comes 3000 to 4000 ms after the rig's marker. The first non-empty detail appears 1900 to 3000 ms after Cancel. Nothing shows before 1.9 s and the line never goes blank from 3 s to the return. The count N is non-decreasing, matches the time since Cancel and uses the pinned wording. NOT RUN by me: it changes the machine's SMB mappings, and the critique's m6 decision allows that at build only with the person's consent, which is not recorded. I checked its analysis against a synthetic log of a correct run and 10 mutants: the good log passed and every mutant failed for its planted reason.

N-001 also asserts the `returned` line's detail is `-`, the final shutdown line's detail is `-`, exit 0, a report written, core.status Cancelled and an OutcomeTitle starting 'Stopped: '. It prints Cancel-to-return as measured and never asserts it. NOT RUN by me, for the same reason as O-004.

StoppingWaitTests.TheWordingAtEachBoundary (Theory: -5 s, -1 ms, 0, 1.999 s, 2 s, 89.999 s, 90 s, 3600 s) and four Facts covering the one-tick boundaries, negative spans, flooring and ASCII with no bound or frequency. All passed in the default run (149/149).

N-002 has two shapes, each on a fresh rig in interactive mode. Shape one: Cancel at +3000 ms, then Close at +5500 ms with the wait line on screen. Shape two: Close at +3000 ms with no prior Cancel. Each asserts the window gone within 1000 ms (hook clock, Window.Closed) and the process gone within 5000 ms (ExitTime against the close's UTC stamp). NOT RUN against the rig. I rehearsed the armed-close path on a local tree with no SMB involved: window gone 4 ms after Close, process 44 ms. CheckCloseEscape passed on that real log and on a synthetic Cancel-then-Close log, and failed each of 5 mutants.

EndStopping is in StartScan's single finally, before ScanningPanel collapses, so the hook's `returned` stamp reads the state after it. The cancelled-cleanly path is fed by C-006 (returned detail `-`) and, opt-in, by N-001. As the design requires, the existing throw and stop cases (C-012, C-006, O-016) pass with the hook's added timer, and all 8 WindowMutants still fail for exactly their planted reason. Not fed by any test: the faulted and finished-on-its-own paths. The shipped exe has no seam that can fault the scan or finish it exactly at Cancel, and the SL-033 rule forbids adding one. Those two rest on the single finally.

Per the accepted M1, the case is replaced by two. N-003: a second run with --wait-sec 2 exits 1 saying another run holds the rig; a third run waits while the first lives; the first run's mapping survives both; every run's mapping is gone at the end. N-004: a run killed without cleanup leaves its mapping behind; the next run starts, sweeps it and serves its own share. The lock itself is proved in the default run by SmbRigTests (passed, including a cross-process kill). N-003 and N-004 were NOT RUN by me because they create and remove SMB mappings.

Isolation is now per server, not per share name. RigLock (named mutex Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig) is held from before the mapping is made until after it is removed. Under it the rig removes only mappings exactly matching \\127.0.0.1\fsa plus 8 hex digits. 'Or on kill' is dropped: the StallRig header says a killed rig cannot clean up and the next run sweeps its leftover. The two replacement cases are N-003 and N-004. Measured along the way: Windows destroys a named mutex with its last handle, so a killed sole holder leaves nothing 'abandoned'. The rig therefore always sweeps rather than relying on that signal.

The rule is now three entries, over tests/**/*.cs, tests/**/*.ps1 and eng/**/*.ps1. The added patterns are \bNew-SmbGlobalMapping\b, (?i)\bnet(?:\.exe)?\s+use\b and \bWNet(?:Add|Cancel)Connection; SmbRig.cs is the only exception. The engine's Fitness check passes: 25 rules, 0 violations, 0 unmatched globs. The patterns fired on planted strings and stayed quiet on Get-SmbMapping.

The minimum fix: the leading \b is dropped from [Ss]can\w*\.WaitAsync\(. I also added \bScan\(.*\.WaitAsync\( for Task.Run(() => Scanner.Scan(...)).WaitAsync(ct). Checked with Python re: _scanTask.WaitAsync(ct), the Task.Run chain and a WhenAny with scan all fire; the legitimate `running.WaitAsync(token)` and the scan's StartNew line do not. Fitness passes on the tree.

An unset FSA_HOOK_CANCEL_DELAY_MS now means no Cancel. Armed stop refuses without it, and armed close without it closes with no prior Cancel (N-002 shape two). WindowCases.ps1 sets 3000 explicitly for N-001 and for N-002 shape one. Rehearsed locally: armed stop with no delay logs 'refused ... armed stop needs FSA_HOOK_CANCEL_DELAY_MS'.

The hook writes a final `stopping ... final=True` line from Dispatcher.ShutdownStarted. It also writes a `returned ms=` stamp when ScanningPanel's Visibility changes; that listener is attached before Cancel is raised, so it fires synchronously in the scan's finally. C-006 and N-001 assert on both lines, and N-001 takes Cancel-to-return from `returned`. Seen in C-006: 'returned ms=12 ... detail=-' then 'stopping ms=66 ... final=True'.

N-001 asserts that no gap between consecutive points exceeds 1000 ms from Cancel (0) to the return, counting every stopping line in between. The hook's timer runs on the UI thread, so a longer gap means a hung UI. A synthetic 1.5 s gap fails it. The statement that the default run proves only that the line does not appear is now in WindowCases.ps1's header, the C-006 comment and SL-020-scanner.md. Not done: having build itself run -IncludeNetwork. The disposition makes that conditional on the person's consent, which is not recorded.

SL-020-scanner.md's decision record says 'Closing the window quits at once' rests on the loopback rig only. The person's protocol now adds, per mode, a run that closes the window while the line shows and times how long until the window is gone and until Get-Process no longer lists the app. The measurement stays with the person, as the disposition says.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 build FsAnalyser.slnx -nologo -v q
tests.note: 0 warnings, 0 errors. The first build after SmbRigTests had 2 xUnit1031 warnings; I fixed them before the final build.
149 passed, 0 failed: the 120 existing plus 29 new (StoppingWaitTests 12, SmbRigTests 17). The SMB-LOOPBACK and TEST-NET-1 traits are still excluded by default.

First run: 1 of 29 failed. The kill test asserted that a killed sole holder's mutex is reported abandoned, but Windows destroys the mutex with its last handle. I removed that signal from RigLock and rewrote the test around a run that waits during the kill. The rerun passed 29/29.
Published the app and built the hook. PASSED all 15 cases (C-001 to C-014, O-016); NOT RUN: N-001 to N-004 (no -IncludeNetwork). Exit 0.
Rerun after moving the SL-038 checks after the ending checks: returned 12 ms after Cancel, no wait line, final line present.
Without -IncludeNetwork this prints 'NOT RUN: N-001 ...' and exits 2 as designed. It proves the not-run reporting only, not the case.

All 8 mutants passed (StopDisabled, StopCollapsed, NoCrashHandler, NoExitRule, CancelThrows, HookFailsAfterActing, HookCompileError, HookLocked). Each hooked case fails for exactly its planted reason with the new hook and checks.

tests.command: <taad3 venv python> -c taad3.fitness.check(<worktree>) after CodeGraph op=rebuild
tests.note: Verdict pass: 25 rules, 0 violations, 0 unmatched, 0 unran, 52 files. The baseline before this build had 3 violations (New/Remove-SmbMapping in StalledShareTests.cs) and 1 unmatched glob (StoppingWait*.cs).

tests.note: The framework-dependent build could not start (exit -2147450730: no machine-wide .NET 10 runtime), so I made it self-contained. After that, bad arguments exit 2 with a usage line. The rig was never started with valid arguments, because that would create a mapping.

tests.command: scratch rehearse.ps1 in %TEMP% (hook armed mode on a local tree, marker written by the script, no SMB)
tests.note: Armed close with no Cancel: window closed 4 ms after Close, process exited 44 ms after. Armed stop: returned and final lines logged. Close after a fast local cancel: refused with 'scan no longer running'. Invalid configurations (stop with no delay, armed throw) refused. A marker that never appears is refused after 60 s. The scratch files are deleted.

tests.command: scratch checks.ps1 in %TEMP% (loads CheckWaitLine and CheckCloseEscape from WindowCases.ps1 by AST, feeds synthetic hook logs)
tests.note: 19 of 19 behaved as expected: 2 good wait logs pass; 10 wait-line mutants fail (line never shown, still shown at return or at shutdown, old wording, count going down, 1.5 s gap, first shown at 3.5 s, shown before 1.9 s, Cancel 1 s after the stall, return inside the gate); 2 good close logs pass and 5 close mutants fail.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case N-001 -IncludeNetwork (and N-002, N-003, N-004)
tests.note: They create and remove SMB client mappings on this machine. The critique's m6 disposition allows build to run -IncludeNetwork only with the person's consent, which is not recorded, and build-check refused the same. The design assigns this run to validate.
Same reason. StalledShareTests now uses the extracted rig; it compiles but was not exercised.

deviations: The wording follows O-002's discharge, not the design. The design's lines were 'Windows usually gives up on its own after about a minute' and, from 90 s, 'This is longer than Windows usually takes'. O-002 (answered after the design) forbids 'usually about a minute' or any other frequency or upper bound, allows 'can take a minute or more', and requires no estimate from 90 s. Built: 'Still waiting for the drive to answer (N s). If a network connection dropped, this can take a minute or more. Closing the window quits at once.' and, from 90 s, 'Still waiting for the drive to answer (N s). Closing the window quits at once.'

Rig isolation follows the accepted M1, not the design's 'pre-removal narrowed to the exact name this run created'. That would remove nothing, and a killed run's leftover could block every later run. Built: a named mutex held for the rig's lifetime, and under it a sweep of mappings exactly matching \\127.0.0.1\fsa plus 8 hex digits. The 'two rig runs at once' case is replaced by N-003 (a second run waits, or fails with an error that says why) and N-004 (a killed run's leftover does not block the next). 'Or on kill' is dropped.

m4 asked for both the final stopping line and the `returned ms=` stamp to come from Closing or ShutdownStarted. The final line does come from ShutdownStarted. The `returned` stamp comes from ScanningPanel's Visibility change instead, because in the close-escape case ShutdownStarted happens while the scan is still stalled, so a stamp taken there would be wrong. The panel's change fires synchronously in the scan's finally, after EndStopping.

StallRig is built self-contained (win-x64). The design said 'built like the hook', but the hook is loaded into the self-contained app, and a framework-dependent StallRig.exe cannot start on this machine: measured exit -2147450730, 'You must install or update .NET', because the only .NET 10 runtime is in the repo-local .dotnet/.

The StallRig contract is extended. It builds its tree in a 'tree' folder next to the --marker file, so a killed run's tree stays inside the case folder that removes it. It also takes an optional --wait-sec (default 150 s) for the rig lock, which N-003 uses to show the fail-with-an-explanation branch.

RigLock reports no 'previous holder died' signal. The first test run measured that Windows destroys a named mutex with its last handle, so a killed sole holder leaves nothing 'abandoned'. Abandonment is only seen by a run already waiting. The rig therefore always sweeps under the lock.

An armed close checks that the scan is still running (ScanningPanel on screen) instead of CancelButton being pressable. After a Cancel the button is disabled, so the design's reuse of 'the same Pressable check' could not express 'Cancel then Close'.
SMBLibrary.Win32 is 1.5.8 in StallRig, not the design's '1.5.8.1 for both'. Core.Tests actually references SMBLibrary 1.5.8.1 and SMBLibrary.Win32 1.5.8, and StallRig matches Core.Tests.

The design leaves these unnamed; I named them. The opt-in window cases are N-001 (wait line), N-002 (close escape), N-003 and N-004 (rig isolation). A network case named without -IncludeNetwork exits 2, so it never reads as passed. I also added default-run SmbRigTests (lock and sweep filter), which prove the M1 fix without a share.
not_built: Nothing in the design was left unbuilt. What was not run: the opt-in cases N-001 to N-004 and the SMB-LOOPBACK StalledShareTests. They create and remove SMB client mappings, and the m6 disposition makes a build-time run conditional on the person's consent, which is not recorded. The design assigns the deliberate -IncludeNetwork run to validate.
C4 (option (a), abandoning the scan thread) is not built. The design retires it if the person accepts (b). C2, the person's acceptance, is still open on design-slice.
follow_ups: Validate (or the person, with consent) runs `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case All -IncludeNetwork` once and records N-001's measured Cancel-to-return. It is the only positive proof that the wait line appears, counts up and clears through the real app. Build proved only the pure function, the negative case and the analysis logic on synthetic logs.
O-001 (owed to validate): the person's 3x3 real-disconnect protocol (Wi-Fi off, `tailscale down`, sleep about 2 minutes), now with one timed Close per mode as documented in SL-020-scanner.md.

The faulted and finished-on-its-own completion paths of the Stopping state have no test feeding them. The shipped exe has no seam to produce them, and the SL-033 rule forbids one. A later slice with an App-level harness could cover them.

Copies of the pre-SL-038 fixture in other worktrees or scratch spike folders take no RigLock. A run of this code can therefore sweep their live \\127.0.0.1\fsa<8hex> mappings if the two run at the same time. This is documented in SmbRig.cs. It goes away once those branches take this rig.

The engine's Fitness import rule ('the stopping wording is a pure function') reports UNRAN until a code graph exists for the tree. It ran here only after CodeGraph op=rebuild. Gates that check a fresh worktree may need the rebuild first.
